meta.title: A Gift for Teacher Kim
meta.textType: functional: an opinion email with reasons, and two advertisements

paragraphs: From: Lily. To: Mia, Leo, and May. Subject: Which gift for Teacher Kim? Dear Mia, Leo, and May, today is Wednesday, March seventeenth. I want to talk about our gift. Farewell Day is on Friday, so we have only two days. At school today, Leo showed us two ads for a gift for Teacher Kim. Now the ads are on my desk next to my laptop.

The first ad is for a notebook and pen set. It is sold at the stationery shop in the shopping center. The shopping center is one mile from our school. The set costs one hundred fifty baht, and that is half price this week. The shop is open every day from noon. The second ad is for a wooden photo frame. It is sold at the old market, next to the bridge. The frame costs two hundred baht. Every frame comes with a free card. The ad says that the frame is for a photo of ten by fifteen centimeters.

Mia took a group photo at the pond last Saturday. Teacher Kim, Mia, Leo, May, and I are in it. Mia gave me a print, and it is on my desk now. I held the photo above my old frame. The old frame is for a photo of ten by fifteen centimeters, too. Mia's photo fits in it well.

In my opinion, the frame is the better gift. I have three reasons. First, Teacher Kim has many notebooks, and she has spare pens in her desk. Second, the frame will hold the photo from the pond, so she can see us every day. Finally, the class box has three hundred baht, and the frame costs two hundred baht. So the total is low, and we can save one hundred baht.

The notebook set has a discount, so it is cheap. But a gift is not only about money. We may spend more on the frame, but she can keep it for many years. The free card is useful, because we can all write a message in it. She might put the frame on her desk at school.

Shall we vote on Thursday after the last Explorers meeting? Then Mia and I can buy the gift on Thursday afternoon. What do you think? This email goes only to you three, because Teacher Kim reads every post of the blog. Best wishes, Lily.
text.summary: Lily writes an email to Mia, Leo, and May about a farewell gift for Teacher Kim. She compares two ads, gives her opinion with three reasons, and asks her friends to vote on Thursday.
